In [[mathematical analysis]], a '''strong measure zero set'''<ref name=Borel/> is a subset ''A'' of the [[real line]] with the following property:
:for every sequence (ε<sub>''n''</sub>) of positive reals there exists a sequence (''I<sub>n</sub>'') of [[interval (mathematics)|interval]]s such that |''I''<sub>''n''</sub>| < ε<sub>''n''</sub> for all ''n'' and ''A'' is contained in the union of the ''I''<sub>''n''</sub>.
(Here |''I''<sub>''n''</sub>| denotes the length of the interval ''I''<sub>''n''</sub>.)

Every [[countable set]] is a strong measure zero set, and so is every union of countably many strong measure zero sets. Every strong measure zero set has [[Lebesgue measure]] 0. The [[Cantor set]] is an example of an uncountable set of Lebesgue measure 0 which is not of strong measure zero.<ref>{{cite book |last=Jech |first=Thomas |author-link=Thomas Jech |year=2003 |title=Set Theory: The Third Millennium Edition, Revised and Expanded |edition=3rd |series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3540440857 |page=539 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WTAl997XDb4C&dq=cantor+set+strong+measure+zero&pg=PA539}}</ref>

'''[[Émile Borel|Borel's]] conjecture'''<ref name=Borel>{{cite journal |last=Borel |first=Émile |author-link=Émile Borel |year=1919 |title=Sur la classification des ensembles de mesure nulle |journal=Bull. Soc. Math. France |doi=10.24033/bsmf.996 |volume=47 |pages=97–125 |url=http://archive.numdam.org/article/BSMF_1919__47__97_0.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref> states that every strong measure zero set is countable. It is now known that this statement is [[independence (mathematical logic)|independent]] of [[ZFC]] (the Zermelo–Fraenkel axioms of set theory, which is the standard axiom system assumed in mathematics). This means that Borel's conjecture can neither be proven nor disproven in ZFC (assuming ZFC is [[consistent]]).
[[Wacław Sierpiński|Sierpiński]] proved in 1928 that the [[continuum hypothesis]] (which is now also known to be independent of ZFC) implies the existence of uncountable strong measure zero sets.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Sierpiński |first=W. |author-link=Wacław Sierpiński |year=1928 |title=Sur un ensemble non denombrable, dont toute image continue est de mesure nulle |language=fr |journal=Fundamenta Mathematicae |doi=10.4064/fm-11-1-302-303 |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=302–4 |url=http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm11/fm11136.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1976 [[Richard Laver|Laver]] used a method of [[forcing (set theory)|forcing]] to construct a model of ZFC in which Borel's conjecture holds.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Laver |first=Richard  |author-link=Richard Laver |year=1976 |title=On the consistency of Borel's conjecture |journal=Acta Math. |doi=10.1007/BF02392416 |doi-access=free |volume=137 |issue=1 |pages=151–169}}</ref> These two results together establish the independence of Borel's conjecture.

The following characterization of strong measure zero sets was proved in 1973:
:A set {{nowrap|''A'' ⊆ '''R'''}} has strong measure zero if and only if {{nowrap|''A'' + ''M'' ≠ '''R'''}} for every [[meagre set]] {{nowrap|''M'' ⊆ '''R'''}}.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Galvin |first1=F. |last2=Mycielski |first2=J. |last3=Solovay |first3=R.M. |year=1973 |title=Strong measure zero sets |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=26 }}</ref>
This result establishes a connection to the notion of '''strongly meagre set''', defined as follows: 
:A set {{nowrap|''M'' ⊆ '''R'''}} is strongly meagre if and only if {{nowrap|''A'' + ''M'' ≠ '''R'''}} for every set {{nowrap|''A'' ⊆ '''R'''}} of Lebesgue measure zero.
The '''dual Borel conjecture''' states that every strongly meagre set is countable. This statement is also independent of ZFC.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Carlson |first=Timothy J. |year=1993 |title=Strong measure zero and strongly meager sets |journal=Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.  |jstor=2160341 |doi=10.1090/s0002-9939-1993-1139474-6 |doi-access=free |volume=118 |issue=2 |pages=577–586}}</ref>
